correctness.rationale: For disjoint bipartite edges, conflict can come only from the two crossed edges; both are absent exactly when the pair transposes two deleted matching indices. Each edge has at most one such disjoint compatible partner. A third edge in a packing containing this pair would therefore have to meet both, but the only bipartite candidates are precisely the two deleted edges. In the remaining case the edges meet pairwise and have one common center: the alternative with three edges is a triangle. Each star subset of size ≥2 has a unique center; the four degree groups give the four binomial terms. The crossed pairs add exactly binom(t,2) at size two. The constant and linear terms are 1 and mn−t. At t=0 the exceptional term vanishes; H_{2,2,2} has only the compatible disjoint pair and enumerator 1+2x+x². The stated max(m,n) is a valid summation cutoff, not necessarily a nonzero top coefficient.
residual_risks: The supplied bounded checks describe 144444 subsets over 32 small triples, another 1048576 subsets for H_{5,5,5}, and 5062 pair comparisons. Larger printed profiles are formula evaluations. The general proof is not contingent on replaying any of these runs.
